predictions.title: Unsolicited asset donation can manipulate vault share price and dilute deposits
predictions.description: WOOFiVaultV2 calculates new shares as amount * totalSupply / balanceBefore, where balanceBefore is the vault's current want balance immediately before the user's transfer. Because unsolicited want-token transfers can increase balanceBefore without increasing totalSupply, an attacker can acquire shares, donate want tokens directly to the vault, and front-run a victim deposit. The victim receives materially fewer shares, while the attacker can later withdraw a disproportionate share of the donated assets and the victim's deposit. The deposit path has no virtual assets/shares protection and no user-provided minimum-share or maximum-price constraint.
predictions.impact: Victim deposits can be substantially diluted or reduced to a near-zero share amount, allowing the attacker to extract part or all of the victim's deposited want assets and any donated assets through withdrawal.
predictions.mitigation: Use virtual assets and virtual shares or another ERC-4626 inflation-attack defense; alternatively maintain internally accounted assets rather than using the raw token balance, and expose deposit minimum-shares/max-price parameters so users can reject manipulated issuance rates.
